title: Algebraic point Weil flag before assigning weights
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, ell different from its characteristic, an algebraic closure Omega of Q_ell, and a compatible geometric point over the sole closed point of Spec(k0). Let F be any raw constructible Omega-Weil sheaf on Spec(k0) [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex; def-weil-constructible-heart]. With the fibre, local operator and flag data of [def-zl-point-weil-flag-data], there exist a flag H and one finite coefficient model T satisfying every clause of the full algebraic flag except purity: finite-dimensional fibre of dimension d, ranks j, zero initial object, terminal isomorphism, all inclusion monos, underlying-heart short exact sequences, one-dimensional quotient fibres with scalar Frobenius alpha_j in Omega units, monotone Frobenius-invariant image spaces and bijective Frobenius on all terms and quotients. T satisfies the entire finite model predicate. Additionally the successive Weil arrows are monos and their Weil-heart cokernels are isomorphic to the specified Q_j. No complex embedding or weight is asserted.

proof.text: Descend F and its inverse Weil structure to one finite coefficient stage using [lem-zl-point-heart-finite-stage]. The point transport is invertible and natural, so the specified local Frobenius is an invertible linear operator compatible with coefficient extension.

Choose a basis and apply [lem-zl-automorphism-flag-finite-coefficients]. The finite overfield contains an adapted flag, quotient lines and their unit eigenvalues. Pass between the actual subfield and its canonical Shrink coefficient model.

Apply [lem-zl-point-equivariant-diagram-lift] to the finite diagram, prescribing the extended original Weil object at its endpoint. Use the specified geometric point and endpoint identifications. This gives all arrows, ranks, invariant images and underlying-heart short exact sequences. The cokernel factorization in the heart is equivariant by its uniqueness after cancelling the Frobenius pullback of the quotient epi; hence these quotients are also Weil-heart cokernels.

Include the entire diagram in the common-stage category. Exact scalar extension and the specified transport comparisons give the finite model equations. In rank zero use the single zero endpoint and no quotients.

theorem zl_point_weil_algebraic_flag
    (F : sfCommonStageWeilSheaf D l hl (zlPointBase D) Ω) :
    ∃ (H : ZlPointWeilFlagDiagram D l hl Ω F)
      (T : ZlPointWeilFlagFiniteDiagram D l hl Ω F H),
      ZlPointWeilFlagAlgebraic D l hl Ω y ι hι F H ∧
      ZlPointWeilHeartFlagModel D l hl Ω y ι hι F H T ∧
      (∀ j, Mono (H.step j)) ∧
      (∀ j, Nonempty (cokernel (H.step j) ≅ H.Q j))
